name: permute
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim from the supplied schema: aten::permute(Tensor(a) self, int[] dims) -> Tensor(a). This representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest calls and results define the full contract for overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and no test may be narrowed, removed or have its reference adapted to fit this one signature. Registered schemas supplied for this operator (all, verbatim): aten::permute(Tensor(a) self, int[] dims) -> Tensor(a). Semantics: permute is a metadata-only, zero-copy relayout view. dims is a required int[] of length equal to the input rank and accepts negative indices (e.g. [-1, -3, -2]); the returned tensor aliases self's storage with strides reordered as stride[d] for d in dims, keeps the same storage_offset, and satisfies _is_view() and equal untyped_storage().data_ptr(). Because it is a view, writes through the result land in the base tensor, lazy conj/neg bits are preserved, and autograd through the operator is a pure exact relayout gradient. Empty dims are valid only for 0-D input ([] gives []), and 1-D input uses [0]. There is no schema default for dims, so omitting it is a missing-required-argument error. The pytest asserts these failure modes only against the candidate: invalid dims (duplicates, out-of-range, negative out-of-range, wrong arity, empty dims for non-scalar input) must raise RuntimeError, IndexError or ValueError, and the omitted-argument form must raise TypeError or RuntimeError; the native operator's own error types are not asserted. Error cases, keyword forms and any additional registered overloads remain owned and exercised by the original pytest.
